title: Apply for a qualified supervisor certificate
summary: Learn about the requirements and process for applying for a qualified supervisor certificate for building and trade work.
intro:
If you want to supervise residential building, and building trade and specialist work contracted for by a licensed contractor, you'll need a qualified supervisor certificate.

A holder of a qualified supervisor certificate is responsible for all work carried out under their supervision, and for ensuring:

A qualified supervisor must be an employee of the licence holder, a member of the partnership, or a director of a company holding the contractor licence.

Certificate applications must be lodged at a Service NSW Centre. You can book an appointment online.
who_can_apply: Eligibility depends on the specific class of work; refer to Licence classes and qualifications for details.
The certificate allows the holder to supervise and carry out the work described on the certificate.
what_you_need: Completed PDF forms (e.g., Application Form - Individual – PDF).
Original or certified copies of qualification requirements (certificates and transcripts).
Certificate of eligibility to obtain insurance (if applicable).

how_to_steps.text: Attend your appointment with your application documents and payment.

more_info.text: Once your certificate has been issued, you can access it digitally through the Service NSW app.
You need a medical gas licence to do any medical gas work in NSW, regardless of the work cost or whether it's residential, commercial or industrial.

faqs.q: Who needs a qualified supervisor certificate?
faqs.a: You need this certificate if you plan to supervise residential building, building trade, or specialist work contracted by a licensed contractor.

faqs.q: Who can be a qualified supervisor?
faqs.a: A qualified supervisor must be an employee of the licence holder, a member of the partnership, or a director of a company holding the contractor licence.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the certificate?
faqs.a: Applications must be lodged at a Service NSW Centre. You can book an appointment online.
